feature: The Story page — `/story/[id]`, the judge screen and home of the discussion layer

problems.problem: THE HEADLINE NUMBER IS INSIDOR'S SCORE, NOT THE USER'S POSITION — and the spec attaches it to a Buy button. `lead_min = (t_crypto - promoted_at)` is a historical fact about the detector. The sticky action bar (desktop shell, 'Sticky action bar') renders `$HORN · $799.6K · +31m early` immediately left of the primary. A user landing four hours after promote reads '+31m early' as a statement about themselves and buys. Nothing on the page renders `now - promoted_at`, which is the only number that tells the reader whether the head start is still theirs. DESIGN.md §3 already defines the correct per-user number — `holding.minutes_early`, 'You got in 41 minutes before crypto traders did' — and this spec never references it. Without it the page proves the company's earliness (marketing) and not the user's (the product), which is exactly the generic-crypto-UI failure mode: strip the +31m and this page is DexScreener with a comment box.
problems.fix: Split the two numbers and never let them share a component. Verdict cell 1 keeps LEAD TIME (+31m, the proof, our record). Add cell 5 or replace the sticky-bar text with YOUR CLOCK: `promoted 4h12m ago · 2 coins since · you are not early` in amber/red, or `promoted 6m ago · no coin yet · you are ahead` in lime, computed as `now - promoted_at` against `count(confirmed)` and `min(mint_time) - promoted_at`. The sticky action bar may show price and ticker; it may never show +31m.

problems.problem: STATE 3 RENDERS N SIMULTANEOUS BUY CONTROLS — the exact state the ONE RULE exists to delete. 'Each row's last cell is a per-row ghost `Buy` chip (`.tbtn-watch` skin, cyan on hover), 28px.' With `BIGGEST` in lime on row 1 and mcap-DESC ordering, the eye resolves to one Buy: the biggest. That is §5.9's 'Buy $TICKER (highest score)' re-implemented as a row control after the spec declares §5.9 superseded. DESIGN.md §1 is explicit that the multi-coin Buy is not a copy problem: 'that state is unrepresentable in the component.' Three Buy chips in a table is maximally representable.
problems.fix: Delete the per-row Buy chip from `.coin-table`. Rows are navigations to `/coin/<mint>` only. The disambiguation happens on the coin page, which is where the trade box lives ('Stories never buy. Coins buy.'). If a compare surface is wanted, take the openQuestion's `/story/[id]/coins` route — but it still cannot carry Buy controls.

problems.problem: `Buy $undefined` IS REACHABLE ON THE PRIMARY BUTTON. `coinState()` gates CONFIRMED on `m.mint_time != null` and nothing else, then builds `` `Buy $${confirmed[0].ticker}` ``. Ticker does not come from `coin_match`; per Q3 it comes from `left join narrative_tickers t on t.mint_ca = cm.mint` — a LEFT join against a table the spec itself documents as deleted and re-inserted every cycle (§5.10 item 10, 'upsertTickers deletes all rows each cycle'). Any page load racing an enrichment cycle returns a CONFIRMED match with a null ticker row. Same path nulls MCAP/LIQ, which then silently reorders the table and breaks the `mcap[0] >= 2 × mcap[1]` BIGGEST comparison.
problems.fix: Add G1b to the CONFIRMED filter: `m.ticker != null && m.mint != null`. Denormalise `ticker` and `name` onto `coin_match` at match time so the button never depends on a truncate-and-reinsert table. Define the null-mcap ordering explicitly (nulls sort by mint_time ASC into the FIRST position, not last) and make the 2× rule return 'no row badged' whenever either mcap is null.

problems.problem: THE POSITION BADGE CANNOT BE COMPUTED FROM THE API IT CITES. `api/balance.js` (read at /api/balance.js) returns `{ sol, token }`: `sol` is `getBalance(owner)/1e9` — the wallet's NATIVE SOL, entirely independent of `mint`; `token` is a summed `uiAmount` (decimals already applied). The spec writes `lamports = await balance(user.wallet_address, mint)`, branches on `lamports > 0`, and formats `(lamports/1e9).toFixed(1)` as `holds 2.1 SOL`. Three separate failures: (a) branching on `sol` renders 'holds' for every commenter, since a connected funded wallet is required to post — a fabricated credential on 100% of comments, the precise harm §5 says must never happen; (b) branching on `token` and dividing by 1e9 is wrong twice over — it is not lamports and pump.fun mints have 6 decimals, so 2,100,000 $HORN renders `holds 0.0 SOL`; (c) SOL-denominating a token position requires a price quote the spec never fetches. Additionally the route returns HTTP 200 on every error via `okJson` (api/_lib/http.js:7), so 'read failed → position unknown' cannot key off status, and it makes two sequential Helius RPC round trips inside the claimed 800 ms budget — on the comment POST path, blocking the user's post.
problems.fix: Store what you can actually read: `snap_position_raw bigint` (the token account raw amount), `snap_position_decimals int`, `snap_position_mint text`. Render `holds 2.1M $HORN`, not SOL — the denomination the user actually holds and the one that needs no price. Treat `{token: null}` or a non-null `error` field as 'position unknown'. Fetch Helius directly server-side with an AbortController, not through the open CORS proxy, and make the read fire-and-forget with a single UPDATE that the immutability trigger whitelists once.

problems.problem: SUPABASE REALTIME BROADCASTS BLOCKED AND SILENTLY-DROPPED COMMENTS TO EVERYONE. Q6 subscribes to `postgres_changes` INSERT on `comment` filtered only by `narrative_id=eq.<id>`. Q4's `status='visible' or author_id=$me` is a read-path filter and has no effect on the replication stream. Every row written by §6 rule 1 (`status='removed'`, address gate) and rule 4a (silent drop, 'appears in their own feed and nowhere else') arrives live in every connected client's feed. The address-gated row's payload is a contract address under a hot story — the exact impression the spammer paid for, delivered faster than an unmoderated feed would have.
problems.fix: Do not use `postgres_changes` on `comment`. Either add an RLS policy on the realtime publication that filters `status='visible'` (and confirm it applies to the replication slot on your Supabase version), or broadcast from the insert handler on a server-owned channel after the status check, sending only the sanitised visible row. Test rule 4a end-to-end: post the same body under three stories in ten minutes with a second browser open.

problems.problem: THE MOST IMPORTANT TRANSITION ON THE PAGE IS UNSPECIFIED: the story gaining its first coin while the user is looking at it. STATE 1 → STATE 2 is the moment the entire product exists to occupy, and `coin_match` has no realtime channel, no poll interval, and no revalidation contract anywhere in the spec (only `comment:<narrative_id>` is subscribed). Both outcomes are bad and neither is chosen: stale means the user clicks 'Create coin' on a story that minted eight minutes ago and pays to create a duplicate of a coin the page is hiding from them; live means the cyan primary swaps from 'Create coin' to 'Buy $HORN' under a finger already travelling, dropping them into a buy flow for a coin they never evaluated.
problems.fix: Subscribe `coin:<narrative_id>` alongside the comment channel. On the first CONFIRMED arrival do NOT mutate the primary in place: freeze the existing button, render a 44px cyan interstitial above the coin section — 'A coin was just made for this story. $HORN, 40 seconds ago.' with an explicit 'Show it' — and require a click before the coin section re-renders. Same pattern for a coin appearing while the create sheet is open. Also gate `/create?story=<id>` server-side on a fresh `count(confirmed)=0` check at submit.

problems.problem: THE STALE-PIPELINE DETECTOR WOULD HAVE READ 'LIVE' THROUGH THE OUTAGE THAT KILLED THE SITE. §9 specifies `stale = (now - max(worker_cycle_log.ran_at)) > 10 min`. `worker_cycle_log` has a `worker` column with at least four writers — `ingest`, `ingest-tiktok`, `snapshotter`, `trends` (worker/lib/cycle-log.js:3, worker/ingest.js:733, worker/snapshotter.js:376, worker/trends.js:257). DESIGN.md §2 documents the live failure exactly: X ingestion died 2026-07-25 08:54, `display_eligible` fell to zero, and 'snapshot and trends crons are still firing normally... but do 0 calls · 0 tweets'. `max(ran_at)` was fresh the entire time. The one detector protecting every number on this page is blind to the only outage that has actually happened.
problems.fix: Per-worker freshness with per-worker thresholds, plus a work-done check: stale if `latestCycle('ingest').ran_at < now-10min` OR `sum(ingested) over the last 6 ingest cycles = 0` OR `latestCycle('snapshotter').snapshots_written = 0` across the last 3 cycles. `latestCycle(sb, worker)` already exists in worker/lib/cycle-log.js:19 and already selects `ingested` and `snapshots_written`. Band copy names the dead lane: 'X ingestion last produced a post 34 minutes ago.'

problems.problem: THE STAMP'S ONE DECORATED TOKEN IS THE ONE THING THAT IS NOT IMMUTABLE. §4 states 'It is a historical fact and is never recomputed. No joins at read time', enforced by a BEFORE UPDATE trigger — and then defines `isEarly(c) = c.snap_coin_count === 0 && c.snap_views <= 0.25 * narrative.combined_views_now`, a read-time comparison against a live column, i.e. a join, recomputed on every render. A comment written at 340K views on a 1M-view story (34%) carries no tag; the story grows to 2.4M and the same comment retroactively becomes `· early`. The badge drifts monotonically in the author's favour over time, which is the precise defect §5 refuses to accept for the position badge ('a false sold is a fabricated credential').
problems.fix: Freeze it like everything else: `snap_early boolean`, computed once at insert against `combined_views` as read in step 4 of Q5, written with the other five snap_ columns and covered by the same immutability trigger. If the ratio must stay live, drop the `· early` token entirely — a stamp that changes is worse than no decoration.

problems.problem: THE ADDRESS GATE HAS A DELIBERATE HOLE THAT IS ALSO THE PRODUCT'S HIGHEST-VALUE SHILL VECTOR. §6 whitelists UNSURE mints ('UNSURE mints are allowed... forbidding discussion of what we display would be incoherent'). The abstain band is a design target of 15–30% of matches (D1), so getting a copycat mint into UNSURE is not an exploit, it is the expected path. Chain it: mint a copycat during a hot story → land in UNSURE → the mint is rendered on the page AND its CA passes the gate → post 'ape 4mZq…8xPq before it moves' under the story → readers click 'View anyway' → the /coin handoff is a single checkbox. The stated rationale is self-defeating: because the mint is already displayed with its full readout, allowing the CA in prose adds zero information and only adds the imperative.
problems.fix: Invert the rule. Block every base58 run including this story's own mints — there is nothing a user can say with a CA that they cannot say with `$KANG`, which is already auto-linked. Replace the offending run inline with the ticker chip and let the user post. Keep the loose regex and the asymmetric-cost argument, which are right.

problems.problem: D2 IS SATISFIED IN THE FILTER AND DEFEATED IN THE STATE MACHINE. The outcome band renders only when `lifecycle = DEAD AND now - promoted_at > 24h`. DEAD requires `v < 0.05·v_peak OR (v < 0.2 AND tau > 90)`, where `v` is reshares/min from `narrative_series`, which is built from `post_snapshots` — and snapshots stop when posts are pruned or drop out of the snapshot tier (`narrative_posts.pruned_at`, `snapshot_tier`). When snapshots stop, `v` is NULL, not below a threshold. NULL fails both DEAD predicates, the story never terminates, the nightly job never runs, and the LATE or DUD verdict never enters the public record. Meanwhile the HIT stories — the ones with coins that keep generating snapshot-worthy activity — do reach DEAD and do get scored. The default filter being 'All' is meaningless when a class of misses never becomes a row.
problems.fix: Add a terminal condition that does not depend on the series: `DEAD if last_snapshot_at < now - 6h` (data-starved termination), stored as `lifecycle_reason='starved'` so it is distinguishable. Run the nightly classifier on `now - promoted_at > 48h` regardless of lifecycle, and make an unresolvable story classify as UNMEASURABLE rather than silently pending. Add a monitoring assertion: `count(outcome IS NULL AND promoted_at < now - 72h)` must trend to zero.

problems.problem: GAP DETECTION IS ASYMMETRIC, AND THE UNPROTECTED SIDE IS THE ONE THAT INFLATES THE HEADLINE. `t_crypto = min(t_mint, t_ct)`. `mint_stream_gap` is specced, mandatory, and correctly reasoned. There is no equivalent for the ~300-account crypto-Twitter poller. Two consequences: (1) if the CT poller is down and the mint stream is up, `min()` silently returns `t_mint` and every story where CT was actually first publishes an inflated lead time with no UNMEASURABLE flag; (2) if both are quiet, `t_crypto` is NULL and the page renders `+2h14m and counting` in cyan, live-incrementing every 60 seconds — a growing, animated earliness claim generated by a dead poller. Separately, the codebase already has a second, different definition of 'crypto got here': `ct_pickup` boolean on `narratives`, written by worker/lib/ticker-proposals.js:103 via `isCtPickup()` regex matching. Two definitions of the central claim in one system, and the spec references neither.
problems.fix: Add `ct_poll_gap (started_at, ended_at, reason)` written by the same supervisor pattern, and extend the UNMEASURABLE predicate to `mint_stream_gap OR ct_poll_gap overlaps [promoted_at, t_crypto]`. The `t_crypto == null` render must additionally require both clocks green for the whole window; if either is unverified, show `unmeasurable`, never a counting-up cyan number. Reconcile or delete `ct_pickup` — decide which definition is canonical and say so in the provenance line.

problems.problem: THE ONLY FEE NUMBERS ON THE PAGE ARE THE ONES THAT FLATTER US, AND BOTH ARE UNSOURCED. STATE 1 line 2: 'About 0.02 SOL and 30 seconds. You keep 50% of trading fees, forever.' (a) The 50% split is DESIGN.md §9 decision D2 — explicitly undecided, and §5 marks `payout` as gated on it. (b) The sentence states the creator's share and omits that the other 50% is poster 40 / Insidor 10 — we advertise the user's cut and hide our own on the one page whose thesis is provenance. (c) 'forever' is contradicted by DESIGN.md's own risk register: `sharing_config` permanently disables `collect_creator_fee_v2` for that mint with no fallback collection path. (d) '0.02 SOL' has no source in the dataContract and contradicts the prototype's own 'Cost to launch ~1.02 SOL' (site/index.html). (e) The Buy side — the Jupiter integrator fee of up to 255 bps that we charge on the trade this page's primary button initiates (DESIGN.md F2) — appears nowhere in the spec, not even as a downstream requirement. A page that footnotes its view counts to 41,208 streamed mints and rounds its own revenue share to a marketing sentence is not honest, it is selectively honest.
problems.fix: Until D2 resolves, STATE 1 line 2 reads: 'Creating costs about <X> SOL in rent and fees. Fee split is not final — see how creation works.' with X sourced from a live quote, not a literal. When D2 lands, render all three shares in one mono row: `you 50% · the poster 40% · Insidor 10%`. Add a one-line fee disclosure to the coin-section footer for the Buy path: `Insidor takes <N> bps on trades routed from here` and measure the real Jupiter platform fee first (DESIGN.md Week 0 check 1: docs say 50 bps, live returned 10).

problems.problem: THE MOMENTUM CURVE WILL RENDER A SAWTOOTH AND THE LIFECYCLE SENTENCE WILL READ OFF IT. `narrative_series` does `sum(s.views) ... group by date_trunc('minute', captured_at)` over `post_snapshots`. Snapshots are captured on a per-POST geometric grid (4, 9, 14, 21, 30, 42, 58, 78 min from each post's own arrival), so different posts land in different minutes. Summing whatever happened to be captured in minute t means the story's total views DROP whenever fewer posts snapshotted that minute — the curve oscillates violently and the story appears to die and revive every few minutes. `v`, `v_peak`, `g` and `R-hat` are all derived from this series, so the COOLING predicate ('2 consecutive snaps') will fire on sampling artefacts and the page will print 'Window narrowing. Reshares at 48% of peak' about a story that is accelerating. Two further defects in the same DDL: it is a MATERIALIZED view with no refresh strategy specified anywhere — never refreshed means a frozen chart on a live story, and `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW` is a full recompute across all 52,498+ snapshots, unusable at snapshot cadence — and `to_timestamp(s.captured_at/1000)` assumes `post_snapshots.captured_at` is bigint ms, which docs/schema.md lists only as '(live)' and never verifies.
problems.fix: Last-observation-carried-forward per post before aggregating: a bucketed series where each post contributes its most recent snapshot value as of bucket t, not only the buckets it was sampled in. Use 5-minute buckets (matching the posts/5min series the trigger uses), not 1-minute. Make it a rollup TABLE written incrementally by the snapshotter in the same transaction as the snapshot insert, not a matview. Verify `captured_at`'s real type against the catalog before writing the expression.

problems.problem: THE COIN RANKING IS ANTI-THESIS: mcap DESC systematically demotes the newest coin on a product that sells earliness. `mcap DESC, then mint_time ASC, then liquidity DESC` with `nulls last` in Q3. A brand-new confirmed coin — the one derived from this story, minted four minutes after the post, the coin the entire pipeline exists to find — has no DexScreener index yet, so its mcap is NULL and it sorts BELOW an adopted 41-day-old namesake with $18K. Row 1 gets `BIGGEST` in lime, the earliest gets a small cyan `FIRST`, and the page's own visual hierarchy tells the user to buy the old one. The spec notices the tension ('they are frequently different coins and that fact is worth surfacing') and then resolves it against the thesis.
problems.fix: Default sort `mint_time ASC` — 'the first one made from this story' is at least as sayable as 'the most money in it', and it is the only ordering consistent with the product. Keep BIGGEST as a badge with the 2× rule, drop it as the sort key, and make the printed rule read 'FIRST = made from this story before any other. BIGGEST = most money in it.' Explicitly define null-mcap ordering rather than inheriting `nulls last`.

problems.problem: THE UNVERIFIED HANDOFF HAS NO VERDICT-PRECEDENCE RULE, AND `coin_match`'s OWN PRIMARY KEY GUARANTEES THE CONFLICT. PK is `(narrative_id, mint)`, so one mint carries independent verdicts per story — which is the expected output of a copycat swarm, the stratum §5.10 over-represents in its own eval set. `/coin/[mint]` is a per-mint route. The spec's rule is 'the banner still renders if coin_match.verdict=UNSURE for ANY story linked to this mint', which means a coin CONFIRMED as derived from story A displays a persistent red 'Insidor could not confirm this coin' banner and loses one-tap Buy the moment any unrelated story produces an UNSURE row against it — trivially griefable. The inverse (CONFIRMED anywhere wins) is worse: it hands one-tap Buy to a mint we abstained on for the story the user actually came from.
problems.fix: The banner is a property of the (story, mint) pair the user arrived through, not of the mint. `?unverified=<story_id>` is required for the warning render and the referring story is named in the copy. With no referrer, resolve against the mint's HIGHEST-confidence CONFIRMED story and show the neutral coin page; render a secondary line 'one other story links to this coin and we could not confirm that link' rather than a red banner. Write the precedence into the spec as a table — it is not obvious and it decides whether Buy is one tap.

problems.problem: KILLING THE PERSISTENT RIGHT RAIL ON THIS ROUTE IS THE LARGEST DEVIATION FROM THE SETTLED DESIGN LANGUAGE, AND IT IS ARGUED ENTIRELY FROM THE DISCUSSION COLUMN'S NEEDS. The language states 'A persistent right rail streams live activity with tab modes.' The Story page is where a trader sits longest and where a mint appearing elsewhere is most decision-relevant — no competing terminal hides the tape on its analysis view. Compounding it, the recovery mechanism is wrong: `.rail-reopen` per component-inventory §6.9 is scoped `display:none` → `flex` only under `.shell.token-view.rail-collapsed` (the section is literally titled 'Collapse controls (token view only)'), so it does not exist on this route; and it is `position:fixed; right:0`, so on a page whose right 420px is the discussion column, reopening the rail overlays the composer and the feed.
problems.fix: Keep the rail. Make discussion the rail's fourth tab mode (Chatter is already planned as exactly that in DESIGN.md §4 and buildOrder STEP 6), and promote it to a dedicated column only when `comment_count > 0` and viewport >= 1600px. Otherwise `.story-grid` is `minmax(560px,1fr) 460px-rail` and the evidence column keeps the space. If the rail genuinely must go, extend `.rail-reopen`'s selector to a `.shell.story-view` variant and re-anchor it so it cannot overlay the composer — do not cite an inventory component for a state it does not have.

problems.problem: 420px OF STICKY, FULL-VIEWPORT-HEIGHT DISCUSSION IS ALLOCATED TO THE STORY STATE THAT HAS NO DISCUSSION. On the stories the product exists for — promoted six minutes ago, zero coins, zero comments — the layout dedicates roughly 420 × 830px, about a third of a 1400px page, to 'No takes yet.' and a composer, permanently, while the evidence column is squeezed to its 560px minimum and the narrow breakpoint drops Reposts and Δ30m from the posts table for want of room. The spec's own defence of the page-over-modal decision is that four visible comments is a preview rather than a discussion; the inverse case — zero comments occupying a third of a terminal — is never addressed.
problems.fix: Make the column's width a function of content: 0 comments → collapse to a 52px 'Add your take' strip pinned under the coin section and give the width back to the evidence column (the posts table and momentum chart both use it); >= 1 comment → 360px; >= 8 comments → 420px. The empty-state pre-stamp invitation survives inside the collapsed strip, which is where a first commenter will actually see it — under the action, not beside it.

problems.problem: THE PAGE IS NARRATED WHERE A TERMINAL TABULATES. Count the generated prose: the lifecycle line ('Reshare rate 1.4× this author's own baseline and still climbing. 22 posts in the last 5 minutes, across 2 platforms.'), the lead-time sentence, the outcome band's headline plus body, the UNSURE region's two-line explanation, STATE 1's two lines, the composer's helper text, and four distinct empty states. That is roughly 30 lines of English on a screener whose settled density spec is 'Ranked tables with a rank column... right-aligned numeric columns' and 'uppercase micro-labels at 9-11px'. This is also structurally the pattern design-interaction-model.md §6 item 20 flags as a faked behaviour to be REMOVED: `narrAboutText` / `narrTiming` — 'prose generated from thresholds and presented as analysis'. The spec replaces fake thresholds with real ones and keeps the prose form.
problems.fix: Keep exactly two sentences on the page: the lead-time claim (it is a falsifiable assertion and needs to read as one) and the outcome verdict. Convert the lifecycle line to the density spec's own idiom — a mono row `R̂ 1.40 · v 0.52/min · g +0.020 · 22 posts/5m · 2 platforms` under a Clash 12.5px state word, with the 3px state bar unchanged. Convert the UNSURE explanation to its channel readout plus a single 11px line. The reader is a trader with 5 seconds, and the spec's own job statement says so.

problems.problem: 'BRAND-NEW TOKEN, NO MARKET DATA' CONFLATES TWO STATES AND ENABLES BUY IN THE ONE THAT CANNOT TRANSACT. The spec distinguishes absent from stale ('render `indexing…`') but never distinguishes 'DexScreener has not indexed a pool that exists' from 'no pool exists yet' — a mint created seconds ago on the bonding curve before the first buy, which is precisely the state a story-derived coin occupies during the window this product sells. In the latter case 'Buy stays enabled' sends the user to a trade box where the Jupiter quote returns no route, after they have been told 'No trades yet — you would be the first buyer.'
problems.fix: Three states, not two: `indexing…` (pool exists, DexScreener lagging — Buy enabled), `— · no trades yet` (bonding curve live, quotable — Buy enabled, and verify with a real quote before enabling), `no market yet` (no route from Jupiter — the primary becomes a disabled-with-reason line 'Not tradeable yet. Watch it.' plus the Follow control). Drive it off a live quote probe, not off the absence of a mcap value.

problems.problem: THE DATA CONTRACT TRUSTS `docs/schema.md`, WHICH DESIGN.md EXPLICITLY DOCUMENTS AS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS — and gets both directions wrong as a result. (a) `narrative_tickers.mint_ca` is listed under 'EXISTING — usable as-is'. DESIGN.md §2 states verbatim: schema.md 'lists `mint_ca` on `narrative_tickers`, which does not exist', and the risk register calls the missing mint column 'Blocking F2'. The repo contains a migration that adds it (worker/schema-token-lookup.sql:4) and code that writes it (worker/lib/enrich-tickers.js:22), so whether it is applied to the live catalog is genuinely unresolved — and Q3's join, the ONE RULE's `confirmed[0].mint`, and the address gate's `storyMints` all sit on top of it. (b) `narratives.distinct_authors` is listed as a BLOCKER ('neither is a column in schema.md'). It exists: added in worker/schema-replication.sql:4, written by worker/lib/cluster-persist.js:88, read by site/live.js:793. `author_velocity`, `ct_pickup` and `subject_entity` likewise exist and are likewise absent from schema.md. A spec that ships a fabricated blocker and a fabricated non-blocker from the same bad source has verified none of its data contract.
problems.fix: Regenerate docs/schema.md from the live catalog before STEP 0 — worker/generate-schema-doc.js exists for this. Re-derive the entire 'DOES NOT EXIST' list against the regenerated file. Specifically confirm `mint_ca` presence and backfill state on the live project, and delete `distinct_authors` from the blocker list.

problems.problem: THE SHARE CARD IS THE GROWTH LOOP AND IT IS AIMED AT THE WRONG STORIES WITH THE WRONG ASSETS. `generateMetadata()` emits `og:description = 'We saw this 31 minutes before crypto did. 2.4M views, 1 coin.'` and `og:image = top post media`, with no coinability check. Tier `never` 404s, but tier `no_create` — public tragedy, ongoing disaster (D3) — renders the full page and therefore emits that exact boast, with the disaster's own footage as the card image, into every DM and group chat it is pasted in. The page body carefully says 'Insidor will not help you make a coin from it' while the share card monetises it. Separately, `og:image` hotlinks `narrative_posts.media_url` — a third-party X/TikTok CDN URL that expires, frequently blocks hotlinking, and republishes someone's media under our brand, which sits directly against the X Display Requirements exposure DESIGN.md flags as a hard rule.
problems.fix: Branch the metadata on `coinability_tier`: `no_create` emits title plus 'A story on Insidor', no lead-time claim, no coin count, and a generated placeholder image (the existing `.qthumb .ph` palette rendered server-side), never the source media. For `normal`, generate the OG image ourselves from the palette plus the numbers — never hotlink. And template the description off the real state: a story with a negative lead time currently emits a boast about being early.

problems.problem: THE THIRD NAMED USER — the normie who saw something on TikTok — HAS NO STATE ON THIS PAGE, AND FIRST-RUN IS NOT ENUMERATED ANYWHERE. Every screen's state list covers pipeline and market conditions; none covers 'this human has never used Insidor'. The page as specced presents, unglossed: `+31m` against an unnamed comparison, `R̂`, `reshare rate 1.4× this author's own baseline`, `promoted_at`, `UNVERIFIED CANDIDATES · 2`, `mint`, `LIQ`, `Δ from post`, and a stamp reading 'posted when 340K views · no coin yet · 40m old · early' whose ranking semantics ('Earliest = written when the story was smallest') are explained only in a hover tooltip on a desktop-only control. The one concession to a first-timer is 'About 0.02 SOL and 30 seconds' — which is a number this review has already flagged as unsourced.
problems.fix: Add a FIRST VISIT state to the desktop-shell screen: verdict cell 1 renders a 9.5px `--dim` sub-line 'before the first crypto account mentioned it' instead of the terse comparison label; the coin section's count chip carries a one-time 11px line under it; the discussion header's 'Earliest' definition renders inline rather than on hover for the first session (and on narrow, always — there is no hover on touch). Persist in localStorage, one story only, dismiss on any interaction. Separately enumerate WALLET CONNECTED / NEVER TRADED, which the composer pre-stamp currently renders as 'no position' — a true statement that reads as a judgement on a first-time user.

problems.problem: THE `no_create` TIER LETS US EARN ON A DISASTER WHILE THE COPY SAYS WE WON'T. The coin-section state list: 'COINABILITY = no_create — no primary button is rendered at all. Confirmed coins still list with their per-row Buy chips (a coin that exists can be traded).' Those per-row chips route into a Jupiter swap that pays Insidor an integrator fee. So on an ongoing-disaster story the page renders an amber band saying 'Insidor will not help you make a coin from it', immediately above controls through which Insidor collects a fee on trading exactly that coin. The position is arguable — the coin exists whether or not we route it — but it is unstated, and it is a fee, an abstain and a moral claim colliding in one 44px band.
problems.fix: State it in the band rather than leaving it to be discovered: 'This story is about an ongoing disaster. You can discuss it here. Insidor will not help you make a coin from it. Coins that already exist are listed below and we earn a routing fee if you trade them.' If the founder would not print that sentence, the correct resolution is to suppress the per-row Buy chips on `no_create` too — not to leave the sentence out.

missing: FIRST VISIT / never-used-Insidor — no state anywhere across six screens, despite 'the normie who saw something on TikTok' being one of the three named users. Every term on the page (+31m, R̂, promoted, UNVERIFIED, LIQ, Δ from post, the stamp's ranking semantics) is unglossed.

STORY GAINS ITS FIRST COIN WHILE OPEN (STATE 1 → STATE 2 live) — the single moment the product exists to occupy. No realtime channel on coin_match, no poll interval, no transition treatment, no guard on the create submit.

STORY LOSES ITS COIN / MATCH DEMOTED (CONFIRMED → UNSURE or REJECTED after a re-run) — the reverse transition. The handoff screen covers UNSURE→CONFIRMED ('the banner disappears... the transition is silent') and never the demotion, which is the one that matters: a user is looking at 'Buy $HORN' on a match we have just withdrawn.

WALLET CONNECTED, INSUFFICIENT SOL — the primary is 'Create coin' on 0-coin stories, which costs SOL. Nothing checks balance before the button; the failure surfaces inside the create sheet or at signing.

NARRATIVE MERGED WHILE THE PAGE IS OPEN — cluster-engine merges narratives continuously. The 404 state covers arriving at a merged id (301) but not being on the page when your id is absorbed: the comment channel is on a dead narrative_id, new comments route elsewhere, and the coin section's data stops updating with no signal.

A COMMENT'S STORY GAINS ITS FIRST COIN — every existing stamp reads 'no coin yet' and every position badge reads 'no coin to hold', permanently and correctly, but the discussion column gives no marker of where in the feed the coin appeared. That divider is the single most valuable artefact the stamp mechanic could produce and it is not rendered.

MULTIPLE CONFIRMED COINS AND A POSITION IN THE SECOND ONE — the position badge reads against `confirmed[0].mint` only (openQuestion 11). A commenter holding the #2 coin renders 'no position', which is false in the direction §5 explicitly forbids for a failed read.

COIN_MATCH RUN IS STALE RATHER THAN ABSENT — 'MATCHING NOT YET RUN' covers zero rows and 'Checking for coins…' times out to NONE after 60s, but there is no state for rows that exist and were last computed hours ago while the resolver is down. The page shows a confident 'No coin exists for this story' that is merely old.

THE 4TH+ CONFIRMED COIN — the table shows 3 rows and a '+2 more' row; the '+2 more' row's own behaviour (expand in place, route, anchor) is never specified, and `?coins=open` is described only as arriving pre-expanded.

POSTS TABLE EMPTY / ALL POSTS PRUNED — the single-post cluster case is handled; a cluster whose posts have all been pruned (pruned_at set, rows at .5 opacity) leaves the evidence column with a source post card and a table of ghosts and no statement about what that means for the claim.

DISCUSSION AT SCALE — 'OVERFLOW (>50 comments)' specifies pagination and nothing else. There is no state for a story with 800 comments, where 'Earliest' becomes an archaeology view and the sticky column's own scroll position, the `3 new ↑` pill and the `#c-<id>` permalink scroll interact.

REDUCED MOTION / ACCESSIBILITY — the page specifies nmTickUp/Down animations, a 2s cyan flash on three separate anchors, `pop .4s` arrivals and a 60s live-incrementing counter, with no prefers-reduced-motion state and no keyboard path to the coin section or the sort control.

TOUCH: THE HOVER-ONLY AFFORDANCES — the momentum crosshair has a tap variant, but 'Earliest = written when the story was smallest' (hover), the AUTHORS handle list (title attr), the stamp's exact values (title attr) and the match evidence chip's popover positioning have no touch equivalent, and the narrow screen inherits all four.

THE SHARE CARD FOR A NEGATIVE LEAD TIME — og:description is templated as 'We saw this 31 minutes before crypto did', with no branch for lead_min < 0, unmeasurable, not-promoted or earliness_eligible=false. Three of those five render a boast the page body contradicts.
